incidents.name: Apollo 1
incidents.phase: pre-launch "plugs out" test on the launch pad (AS-204)
incidents.assumed_note: Ventilation speed (10 cm/s) and fuel length (10 mm) are engineering assumptions matching the app presets, not values from a NASA page.
incidents.summary: During a preflight test on the launch pad on Jan. 27, 1967, a fire swept through the AS-204 Command Module, which was pressurized with pure oxygen, and astronauts Grissom, White and Chaffee lost their lives.

sources.quote: On Jan. 27, 1967, astronauts Virgil “Gus” Grissom, Edward White and Robert Chaffee lost their lives during a preflight test for AS-204
during a preflight test for AS-204 when a fire swept through the Command Module (CM).
On Jan. 27, Grissom, White and Chaffee were scheduled to conduct a key test on the launch pad
the spacecraft’s hatches closed and the cabin pressurized with 100% oxygen.
pure oxygen at a pressure of 11.5 newtons per square centimeter (16.7 pounds per square inch) was substituted.

incidents.name: Mir oxygen-generator fire
incidents.phase: in orbit, aboard the Mir space station (Kvant-1 module)
incidents.assumed_note: Mir operated a sea-level-like air atmosphere; cabin pressure (14.7 psia) and oxygen fraction (0.21) are not quoted from a NASA page. Ventilation speed and fuel length are engineering assumptions matching the app presets.
incidents.summary: On Feb. 24, 1997, a solid-fuel oxygen generator ignited in Mir's Kvant-1 module, producing a flame and dense smoke; the station's life support system cleared the smoke over the following hours. Cabin pressure and oxygen here are assumed sea-level air, not values quoted from a NASA page.

sources.quote: On Feb. 24, 1997, the six crew members aboard the Russian space station Mir faced significant danger
when a fire ignited in an oxygen generating system.
as Lazutkin activated a solid-fuel oxygen generator in Mir’s Kvant-1 module, the canister ignited
the worst in-orbit fire incident in the history of spaceflight.

incidents.name: Artemis II smoke alarm
incidents.phase: lunar transit, flight day 9/10 of the Artemis II test flight (date shown is the April 1, 2026 launch)
incidents.assumed_note: No NASA page found giving Orion's cabin pressure or oxygen fraction; sea-level air (14.7 psia, 0.21) is assumed. NASA's thermal report says the alarm turned off the cabin fans, so real airflow was likely lower than the assumed 10 cm/s preset.
incidents.summary: During lunar transit on the Artemis II test flight, a smoke detector alarm that a NASA engineering report later called a false alarm automatically turned off Orion's cabin fans. Cabin pressure and oxygen here are assumed sea-level air, not values quoted from a NASA page.

incidents.name: Apollo 13
incidents.phase: third day of the mission, translunar flight (launched April 11, 1970)
incidents.scope_note: Outside this tool's scope: Apollo 13 was a failure of a high-pressure oxygen tank in the Service Module, not a cabin fire, so the PSI combustion data and this tool do not apply.
incidents.summary: On the third day of the Apollo 13 mission, oxygen tank number two failed, followed by tank number one; the lunar landing was called off and the crew returned to Earth safely.

sources.quote: oxygen tank number two blew up, leading to the subsequent failure of tank number one.
Things went smoothly until the third day of the mission
